findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash() of project IDs, which can collide
findings.body: The key is built from `hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))`. Distinct project sets can in principle produce the same hash, so one set could receive another's cached eligibility. The result would be a wrong upsampling decision, either missing the transform or applying `sample_weight` where it shouldn't be used. `hash()` is also not guaranteed stable across Python versions, and the project IDs should be joined explicitly in the key instead. The same pattern is repeated in `invalidate_upsampling_cache`.

findings.title: Allowlist eligibility cached for 60s and never invalidated
findings.body: The allowlist result is cached for 60 seconds, but `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is never called when the option changes. After an allowlist change, results can be stale for up to a minute. The docstring on `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled` says the option is read fresh to get the latest configuration, which contradicts the caching. The cache saves almost nothing, because `options.get` is already cached in-process.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` is called with the closure variable `dataset`, not `scoped_dataset`. The dashboard widget split logic calls `_get_event_stats` with `discover` or other scoped datasets, and the check ignores them. For example, the errors-only split query `!event.type:transaction` is not detected as an error query. In the other direction, a transaction split can be upsampled when the outer dataset is errors. The check is also repeated for every call.

findings.title: Only count() is transformed; alias "as count" may be unsupported
findings.body: The transform rewrites `count()` to `"upsampled_count() as count"`. Other aggregates, such as `count_unique`, `eps()` and `epm()`, remain un-upsampled. The `as` alias syntax in the column list may not parse in the timeseries query builders. Result key handling for the RPC and top-events paths is also unverified. `upsampled_count` is registered only in the discover dataset, so the errors dataset and the RPC paths may fail to resolve it.

findings.title: Test factory silently swallows exceptions and mutates stored event data
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses bare `except Exception: pass` blocks, which hide errors. It also changes what `store_event` writes for every test that supplies this context. A zero sample rate is silently ignored because of the falsy check.

findings.title: Stray submodule gitlink committed
findings.body: A `sentry-repo` subproject commit entry pointing at the base commit was added. It looks accidental and serves no purpose for this change.
